program.name: Food Assistance Program (FAP) for Legal Immigrants
program.description:
The Food Assistance Program (FAP) helps you buy groceries each month if you are a legal immigrant who cannot get Basic Food (SNAP) because of your immigration status. You get a card that works like a debit card at most grocery stores.

FAP pays the same amount as Basic Food. The amount you get depends on your household size and income. You may qualify if you have a green card but have not had it for 5 years yet, or if you are lawfully present in another way, such as having temporary protected status, being paroled into the U.S., or having a pending asylum application.

You must meet the same income and other rules as Basic Food. People without lawful immigration status cannot get FAP. Select 'Apply Online' to apply through Washington Connection — the same application as Basic Food.
program.description_short: Monthly help buying groceries for legal immigrants who cannot get Basic Food
program.website_description: Monthly assistance to buy food for legal immigrants

warning_messages.message: You might qualify for Basic Food (SNAP) instead of FAP. Two things can make that true. First, you may qualify if you have a green card and you have 40 or more Social Security work credits — credits from a parent, earned while you were under 18, or from a spouse count toward your total. Second, you may qualify if you are a citizen of the Marshall Islands, Micronesia, or Palau, or if you are from Cuba or Haiti and were paroled into the U.S., have a pending asylum application, or are in removal proceedings without a final order. Not sure which program applies to you? Contact DSHS or a caseworker for help.

documents.text: Proof of identity (ex: driver's license, state ID, passport)
Social Security Number for each household member applying
Proof of home address (ex: lease, utility bill, mail with your address)
Proof of income (ex: pay stubs, employer letter, tax return)
Proof of expenses (ex: rent or mortgage statement, childcare bills, utility bills)
Proof of citizenship or immigration status (ex: birth certificate, green card, immigration documents)
